# Khettūpamapetavatthu (Pv 1)

**ID:** Pv 1
**Section:** Petavatthu (pv)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Khettūpamapetavatthu
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0507m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khettūpamapetavatthu* ("The Simile of a Field", Pv 1) is the opening story (*vatthu*) of the canonical *Petavatthu* [Norman 1983]. Unlike many stories in the collection that follow a conventional narrative dialogue between an observer and a suffering spirit (*peta*) recounting past misdeeds, the text appears to have been included simply because it incorporates the word *peta* [Norman 1983]. It conveys the teaching that arahants are like a fertile field wherein offerings can be planted, and that honouring arahants and *petas* is like planting seeds that will produce a corresponding karmic reward (*phala*) in due course [Norman 1983].

**Sources**

- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pali Literature (1983) — Identification as the first story of the Petavatthu, doctrinal content on honouring arahants and petas as planting seeds to receive karmic reward, and context within the collection.
